title: Sensory fibers among immune cells
objective: Interpret imaging of CGRP+ fibers alongside immune cells in the gut wall.

steps.title: What the slide shows
steps.body: Stain the colon wall for a sensory marker ([[CGRP]]) and an immune marker (CD45) and you see varicose nerve fibers running through the [[lamina propria]] with immune cells clustered right beside them — often close enough to signal. Proximity is the first clue to interaction.

steps.prompt: CGRP+ fibers and CD45+ immune cells sit immediately adjacent in the gut wall. What does that *suggest* (not prove)?
options: They are positioned to signal to each other locally
They must therefore be the very same cell type
Neither cell can respond to the other one at all
The tissue must simply have been fixed incorrectly
steps.explanation: Adjacency suggests the opportunity for local signaling; proving it needs functional tests (receptors, silencing). CGRP marks nerve fibers, CD45 marks immune cells — different cell types sitting close.

variants.setup: Sensory fibers and immune cells lie side by side in the wall.
options: An opportunity to signal, but not proof of it
That the two are really the same cell type
That the two simply cannot interact at all
variants.reveal: Proximity suggests possible signaling; function must be tested separately.

steps.setup: You want to move from 'they're close' to 'they signal'.
steps.prompt: What would show a functional link?
options: Removing a receptor or silencing the neurons changes the immune cells' behavior
Simply taking a much higher-resolution picture of the two cells side by side
Counting how many immune cells are present across the whole gut wall
Showing that fiber density rises wherever immune cell numbers rise
steps.reveal: Function needs a perturbation: knock out the receptor (e.g. RAMP1) or silence the neurons and see the immune readout change. Imaging locates the players; experiments prove the link.

variants.prompt: To prove sensory fibers signal to nearby immune cells, you'd…
options: Perturb the receptor or silence the neurons, then measure the response
Take a sharper, higher-magnification image of the two cells together
Count up all of the immune cells across the entire gut wall
variants.explanation: A functional perturbation, not better imaging, proves the link.

sources.note: DRG afferents in the colon wall, among lamina-propria immune cells.

reviewNotes: CGRP/CD45 proximity; proximity vs function; ties to B8 colon slide.
